newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 24.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Dr Michael Simpson, writing in the latest edition of Hospital Doctor magazine says that 'the ability of carer or carers to bond with the baby and thus promote contented sleep is vital to much of Sudden Death Infant Syndrome. He also stresses that it is the erratic care provided by mothers who smoke that increases the risk factor of cot deaths.
HALIFAX TO GIVE UP TAKEOVER PROTECTION

Following its flotation on the stockmarket next June, the Halifax building society is to forgo current building society legislation by abandoning its right to five years of takeover protection. The move is likely to increase pressure on other building societies planning to go public, to open themselves to the toughest stock market test: trial by takeover approach.
AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL SELL-OFF IS GROUNDED

The Department of Transport is expected to announce a delay in the privatisation of Britain's air traffic control service next week. The controversial sale could have raised an estimated 600 million stg.
CABBIES STEER A COURSE FOR 10 MLN STG FLOTATION

Computer Cab, London's black cab drivers who formed a radio network to fight off competition from minicabs is to float on the Alternative Investment Market next month if it receives approval of 5000 members of the London Taxi Drivers' Association. Under the plan the LTDA would keep a 60 percent majority shareholding. The company would be valued at between 8 and 10 millin stg.
ITV BID TO BRING BSKYB INTO THE TAX NET

Independent television companies are increasing pressure for major change in the TV licensing system to bring BSkyB within the broadcasting tax bracket for the first time. It is proposed that the levy system be scrapped and replaced by an advertising tax that would apply to all broadcasters.
